questions.title: Highest Share of Structurally Deficient Bridges
questions.current_disclaimer: Share of a state's public road bridges rated in Poor condition under the FHWA NBI (formerly 'structurally deficient').

questions.title: Most High-Hazard-Potential Dams
questions.current_disclaimer: High-Hazard-Potential dams are those whose failure would likely cause loss of human life, regardless of dam size or current condition.

questions.title: Highest Public Transit Ridership per Capita
questions.current_disclaimer: Unlinked passenger trips per resident, all reported transit modes. State totals derived from NTD agency reports.

questions.title: Highest Average Gasoline Price
questions.current_disclaimer: State average price per gallon of regular unleaded. Prices reflect state-level taxes, transportation costs, and fuel-blend requirements.

questions.title: Most Freight Rail Miles
questions.current_disclaimer: Route miles of freight railroad (Class I, regional, and short line), not track miles. Route mileage counts a rail corridor once regardless of parallel tracks.

questions.title: Most National Historic Landmarks
questions.current_disclaimer: Landmarks that span more than one state are counted once for each state they touch, so state totals include a small amount of double-counting.

questions.title: Most National Natural Landmarks
questions.current_disclaimer: A handful of landmarks span two states and are counted for each state they touch.

questions.title: Highest Peak Inside a National Park
questions.current_disclaimer: Only formally designated National Parks are counted (not National Monuments, Preserves, or Recreation Areas). Multi-state parks are credited to the state where the highest in-park summit lies.

questions.title: Largest Fully In-State Lake by Surface Area
questions.current_disclaimer: Excludes lakes that cross state or international borders (Great Lakes, Lake Champlain, Lake Tahoe, Lake Powell, Kentucky Lake, Toledo Bend, Lake Mead, etc.). Great Salt Lake and Salton Sea are included despite being saline.

questions.title: Highest Forest Cover Percentage
questions.current_disclaimer: Percent forested is computed on land area only (excluding inland water). US territories such as American Samoa are excluded from this state-only ranking.

questions.title: Most Counties or County Equivalents
questions.current_disclaimer: County-equivalent divisions (parishes, boroughs, and independent cities) are counted alongside counties. States that combine a county and an independent city count both.

questions.title: Greatest Elevation Range Within a State
questions.current_disclaimer: Range equals the state high point minus the state low point. States with sub-sea-level low points get a small boost in range from the negative minimum.

questions.title: Largest State Fair by Attendance
questions.current_disclaimer: Only official single-state fairs are counted here; regional/multi-state exhibitions (such as the New England Big E) are excluded.

questions.title: Most Total Forest Land Area (Acres)
questions.current_disclaimer: Measures absolute forest land in acres, not percent of state forested. FIA counts all forested land (public, private, and tribal).

questions.title: Most Wilderness Acreage
questions.current_disclaimer: Wilderness areas that cross state boundaries have their acreage split by state. Six states (Connecticut, Delaware, Iowa, Kansas, Maryland, Rhode Island) contain no designated wilderness.

questions.title: Most National Wildlife Refuges
questions.current_disclaimer: Refuges that span two states are attributed to the state where the main visitor entrance is located. Wetland Management Districts (in some Midwestern states) are included alongside refuges.

questions.title: Most Ski Areas
questions.current_disclaimer: Includes all ski areas with lift-served terrain, from major destination resorts down to small local hills. Only 37 US states host any operating ski areas.

questions.title: Most Long Rivers (500+ Miles) Passing Through
questions.current_disclaimer: A river is credited to every state it flows through, whether as source, mouth, or intermediate section. Only main-stem rivers 500 miles or longer are counted.

questions.title: Largest Total National Park Acreage
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts only formally designated National Parks (not monuments, preserves, or historic sites). Multi-state parks have their acreage split at the state boundary.

questions.title: Most Public Aquariums
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts standalone aquariums plus aquarium sections of zoos and science centers as listed in the source. Includes both open and recently closed facilities.
